newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Amsterdam port traffic up 7.3 pct in first half.
newsitem.headline: Amsterdam port traffic up 7.3 pct in first half.

text.p: Amsterdam area port traffic rose to 26.9 million tonnes in the first six months of the year, up 7.3 percent on the same period in 1995, the port authority said on Wednesday.

It said all sectors had shown a positive result, making Amsterdam the only port in the Benelux region to show growth. Earlier this month its far larger competitor Rotterdam posted a 1.8 percent fall in first half turnover to 143 million tonnes.
Godfried van den Heuvel, director of the Amsterdam Port Authority, said he expected full-year turnover in 1996 to exceed 1995's record of 50 million tonnes.
Shipments of dry bulk in the first half rose 8.4 percent to 18.4 million tonnes, among which coal was up 23.7 percent to 5.8 million and agribulk up 24.3 percent to 4.6 million tonnes.
The port handled 4.7 million tonnes of liquid bulk. 3.2 percent more than last year. Oil products were up 4.2 percent to 3.3 million tonnes and crude oil 7.2 percent up at 0.49 million.

The general cargo sector rose 7.6 percent to 3.8 million tonnes. Container traffic grew by a hefty 55.2 percent to almost one million tonnes but the ro-ro sector declined 32.6 percent to 0.26 million tonnes.
Despite increased use of containers for shipping cocoa, conventional (bagged) general cargo shipments still rose by 2.7 percent to 2.6 million tonnes, the port said.
The figures cover transshipments handled by the ports of IJmuiden/Velsen, Beverwijk, Zaanstad and Amsterdam.
